content:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT: PolarForge PROD - spike of 429s observed on Dedicated pool PF-DED-01. Pagerduty triggered for oncall.

jessica: I’m on it. Can someone confirm scope? PF reported errors starting ~10m ago.

mike: Seeing elevated 429 counters on PF-DED-01 / tenant polarforge-prod. Rate limiter logs: 
```
RATE_LIMIT_REJECT tenant=polarforge-prod count=1243 window=60s reason=contract_quota
```

ryan_oncall: Paging in. Is this contract quota or a bug in the limiter?

lisa-eng: Customer says they launched a big batch job — seems like sudden ramp. They’re on a reserved Dedicated pool, quota should be higher.

jessica: Confirmed: token usage for that tenant jumped 6x. Dedicated pool hit a per-tenant soft quota (config: `tenant_max_burst=1000/min`) that we enforce to protect isolation. Looks like it throttled correctly but customer needs immediate relief.

beth-cs: Customer (PolarForge) on the line: "This is blocking checkout flows, >30% 429s for our users." They need mitigation ASAP.

mike: Options: (1) temporary contract override (emergency lift) for polarforge-prod, (2) move traffic to Hosted fallback models for a subset of requests, (3) increase tenant_max_burst on PF-DED-01. I can do 3 quickly if approved.

jessica: I can execute 3 (local config change) but want to avoid destabilizing other tenants. We should confirm other tenants' headroom. Running quick query on pool headroom.

mike: Running: `SELECT tenant, active_tokens_per_min FROM pool_metrics WHERE pool='PF-DED-01'` — results show other tenants at 10-40% of their quota. Headroom available.

ryan_oncall: I'm 👍 for an isolated temporary increase on their tenant config while we coordinate with billing. Jessica, proceed with a conservative raise: `tenant_max_burst=3500/min` for 20 minutes, then auto-downscale to 1000 if no rollback.

jessica: Executing now. Patch command: 
```
admin-cli tenants update --id=polarforge-prod --set tenant_max_burst=3500 --pool PF-DED-01
```
Applying...

pagerduty-bot: jessica acknowledged the incident.

lisa-eng: Patch applied, confirming metrics... 429s dropping from 32% -> 4% in last 90s. Customer confirms partial recovery.

beth-cs: PolarForge: "Traffic stabilizing, but please keep us posted on duration and eventual billing impact."

mike: We should still offer a hosted fallback option for non-critical workloads — can route low-priority inference to hosted models to reduce burst. Doing a quick routing rule: 
```
routing-cli create --from tenant=polarforge-prod --to hosted-economy --match tag=async --priority=low
```

jessica: Doing a final verification on pool latency/queue depth. All good. Setting auto-rollback timer: 20 minutes.

billing-bot: Billing alert created: ticket #BILL-4821 for emergency quota override review. Charge estimate sent to account team.

ryan_oncall: Handing off to overnight oncall (mike) in 25m. Action items for handoff: 1) monitor auto-rollback at +20m 2) escalate to leadership if error rate >5% after rollback 3) confirm billing ticket resolution tomorrow.

mike: Acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor. Also creating a short-lived canary to ensure new config is stable: 
```
admin-cli canary create --tenant polarforge-prod --pool PF-DED-01 --samples 50
```

jessica: Canary passed. Queue depths normal. Recording incident log entry and tagging for postmortem: "tenant_quota_activation, emergency_lift, routing_fallback_used"

beth-cs: Customer asked about a permanent contract change. I’ll open a renewal conversation and link BILL-4821.

lisa-eng: Note: we should consider adding an automated suggestion in Redwood Optimize to detect sudden ramp and pre-authorize short emergency lifts for dedicated tenants with known renewal talks. Filing RFC ticket.

pagerduty-bot: Incident status: mitigated (partial) — 429s reduced below major threshold.

mike: Auto-rollback time reached, reducing tenant_max_burst -> 1000 (rollback script executed). Monitoring...

jessica: After rollback 429s remained under 1.5% for the last 5 minutes. Good.

beth-cs: PolarForge confirms they’re back to normal. They requested a 1:1 tomorrow to discuss permanent uplift.

ryan_oncall: Closing incident from oncall perspective. Please add a postmortem with timeline, root cause (customer ramp + strict tenant quota), decisions, and billing follow-up. Assign to jessica + beth.

jessica: Will draft postmortem. Adding runbook updates to clarify emergency lift steps and criteria.

billing-bot: BILL-4821 updated: awaiting account team sign-off on chargeable emergency override; no automatic charge until approval.

mike: Closing thread. Thanks all for quick turnaround :thumbsup:
